pr.title: perf(moe): one persistent DeepSeek FP8 activation kernel for the trtllm-gen MoE
pr.body:
## 📌 Description

### Summary

The trtllm-gen fused MoE runs a separate activation kernel between its two expert GEMMs when the model uses DeepSeek FP8 block scaling: SwiGLU plus re-quantization of GEMM1's output to e4m3 with one scale per 128 columns. The existing kernel, `activationDeepSeekKernel`, launches one block per column block of every (token, top-k slot) pair, packing 2 or 4 tokens into a block at larger token counts, and its time grows with tokens × top-k even though, under expert parallelism, most of those slots belong to other GPUs. This PR replaces it, for the fused MoE, with one persistent kernel that launches at most 8 blocks per SM and decides on the device, from the live row count that routing produced, how to split the work. For finite inputs the kernel writes exactly the same bytes as the old one, and both kernels drop a NaN from GEMM1 alike (see Correctness).

Measured inside the fused MoE call on two exclusively allocated cluster nodes, a B300 (sm_103) node and a Vera Rubin (sm_107) tray (tables below; speedups are before / after; 1 to 128 tokens are the headline range, 256 tokens and above are context rows): with PDL off, so that the profiler reports the kernel's own time, the activation is 1.2x faster at 1 token (no local pair on this rank, so the kernel exits on an empty list), 0.88x to 0.95x at 2 and 4 tokens and at 8 tokens on the sm_107 tray (0.1 to 0.3 us slower; its one-round-trip schedule pays off only when the launch overlaps GEMM1), 1.00x to 1.09x otherwise at 8 and 16 tokens, 1.3x to 2.5x faster at 32 to 128 tokens, and 3.2x to 13.2x in the context rows from 256 to 2048 tokens. With PDL on, the production launch mode, the whole fused MoE call at EP8 is 1.00x to 1.06x at 1 to 16 tokens, inside the 1 to 2 % control drift except on the B300 at 4 and 8 tokens (1.04x and 1.03x), 1.02x to 1.04x faster at 32 to 128 tokens and 1.05x to 1.40x in the context rows from 256 to 2048 tokens. End to end in vLLM 0.32.0 on 8x B300 (GLM-5.3, TP8 attention + EP8 MoE, two baseline / patched pairs, each on one exclusive node, section below), the decode step is 1.5 % shorter at 128 and 144 concurrent requests (2.4 % at 256, a context row), inside the pairs' drift at 64 requests and below, and a 16K-token prefill chunk is 8.3 % shorter; held at the baseline's interactivity instead, the patched build carries fewer than 16 more requests at 128 and at 256 by the measured points (about 5 and 2.4 % more by interpolation between them); per MoE layer the activation's exclusive time falls from 6.0 to 1.9 us at 64 requests and from 823 to 38 us in the prefill chunk. The old kernel stays for the one caller that does not provide the row map (the standalone activation op).

### What changes

- `csrc/fused_moe/trtllm_backend/trtllm_fused_moe_dev_kernel.cu`: the new kernel `activationDeepSeekKernelPersistent128` and its host side; `activation::run()` selects it whenever `persistentActivationSupported()` holds (row map and bound present, 128-wide scale blocks, whole blocks per row, 16-byte aligned buffers, and the tile → expert map when the per-expert SwiGLU controls are set), else the old kernel as before.
- `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fused_moe/DevKernel.h`, `csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_runner.cu`: `activation::Data` carries the permuted row → token map and the padded-row bound, set by the runner from its workspace.
- `csrc/trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu`: with PDL on, a check that a kernel the interface launches with the PDL attribute (one with any grid-dependency wait or fine-grained-consumer flag) waits on its primary and cannot trigger its dependent launch or exit before that wait, the property the glue kernels' pre-wait reads rely on. It holds for all 8350 kernels of the pinned manifest.
- `tests/moe/test_trtllm_gen_moe_activation_persistent.py` (new): the fused MoE launches the persistent kernel, and only it, at 1, 8, 64 and 1024 tokens with all experts local and with a quarter local, PDL on and off; PDL on and PDL off produce identical bytes at 1, 8, 64 and 512 tokens, with and without per-expert SwiGLU controls; under expert parallelism (a quarter of the experts local, where the kernel walks the permuted rows and resolves each row's expert through the tile map) the output matches the dequantized reference at 8, 32 and 64 tokens, with and without per-expert controls (at 8 tokens the padded row count is at most the pair count, so the kernel takes the rows list at or just inside its boundary; at 32 and 64 tokens it takes it with margin, the padded rows being about half the pairs at the default tiles); a rank with no (token, slot) pair at all gets an empty work list and an all-zero, PDL-independent output.
- `tests/moe/test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py`: the DeepSeek FP8 SwiGLU-controls test also checks distinct per-expert values against the reference, with neighbouring experts far apart so that a lookup off by one GEMM tile would fail the comparison.

No Python API change; `activation::Data` gains two fields with defaults, so other callers of `activation::run()` are unaffected.

### How the kernel works

A *piece* is one 128-column scale block of one permuted row. 32 lanes of a warp own a piece when there are few pieces (4 bytes per lane, 5 xor-shuffles for the block maximum) and 8 lanes when there are many (16 bytes per lane); no shared memory, no block barrier. Every block strides over a work list, and the kernel picks the list on the device: the permuted rows (skipping padding rows) when the live padded row count P is at most the number of (token, slot) pairs, else the pairs (skipping pairs routed to other GPUs). Neither padding nor remote pairs cost a data load. The list entry of a piece is fetched two pieces ahead and its data one piece ahead, so each piece costs one memory round trip.

P, the two index tables and the tile → expert map are routing outputs, and the kernel reads them before its PDL wait: GEMM1, the kernel it depends on, waits on routing in every CTA before it triggers or exits, and `griddepcontrol.wait` returns only when routing has completed with its writes visible, so those tables are final whenever this kernel runs. GEMM1's output is read only after the wait. The per-expert SwiGLU controls (alpha, beta, clamp) are looked up once per piece instead of once per element.

### Correctness

- Bit-identical to `activationDeepSeekKernel` on every live row and scale in a standalone harness: 150 configurations with the 128-wide scale block in the prototype's final revision (GLM and Qwen shapes, 8- and 64-row GEMM tiles, EP8 and EP1, 1 to 2048 tokens, with and without per-expert controls), plus 48 with the 32-wide block that is not compiled here; padding rows are left untouched, as the old kernel leaves them.
- Inside the fused MoE, the `main` build and this branch produce bit-identical outputs (the final output and the GEMM2 rows of every local pair) in all 11 cases of a module-level comparison on an sm_107 board: the GLM-5.3 shape on EP8 rank 3 at 1, 7, 49, 50, 64, 256, 2048 tokens; the GLM-5.3 shape on EP8 rank 0 at 7, 256 tokens; a shape with five scale blocks per row (intermediate 640) on EP8 rank 1 at 7, 256 tokens.
- Module tests: the new test file (40 cases) passes on sm_100 and sm_107 boards; the DeepSeek FP8 SwiGLU-controls test, the Prims-TS (the explicit unified-MoE backend described in `docs/api/fused_moe.rst`) block-scale test and the renormalize-FP8 routing file pass; the new test skips on other architectures.
- Numerics are the old kernel's operation for operation. The block maximum is reduced with `fmaxf`, as the old kernel's 2- and 4-token instantiations do; its 1-token instantiation reduces with `cuda::maximum<>`, which the vendored CCCL implements as `fmax` for float (a hardware `redux.sync.max` on the sm_100a / sm_100f builds), so all three reductions drop a NaN alike and no difference is expected for a NaN input either; the bitwise comparisons used finite inputs.

### Performance

Problem: `trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe` as vLLM calls it for GLM-5.3 at EP8: hidden 6144, intermediate 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8, DeepSeekV3 routing with bias, one rank's 32 local experts (`local_expert_offset` 96) so one in eight (token, slot) pairs is local, CUDA graph replay; routing logits are drawn on the device with a fixed seed, and the draw differs between the two environments from 512 tokens up, hence the different local-pair counts there. 1 to 128 tokens are the decode range and the headline; 256 to 2048 tokens are context rows (beyond the headline range, not the prefill phase).

**Reproducible benchmark.** The repository benchmark, baseline (`main` at the merge base) and this branch alternating three times on the exclusively allocated sm_107 tray, whole call by CUDA events. Two of its limits shape the configuration: its reference routing needs `topk_group × n_group ≥ top_k`, so DeepSeek-V3's grouping (8 groups of 32 experts, 4 chosen) stands in for GLM's single group, and it allocates weights for every expert, so all 256 experts are local here (every (token, slot) pair is local, the EP1 case; the EP8 case follows in the tables below).

### End to end: GLM-5.3 in vLLM 0.32.0 on 8x B300 (two same-node baseline / patched pairs; step times measured, percentages derived from the tables)

**Setup.** Two pairs, each on one exclusively allocated 8x B300 node of the same cluster (a different node per pair), the baseline arm first and the patched arm right after it on the same node, so that node-to-node differences cancel within a pair (driver 580 with the CUDA 13.2 forward-compatibility user-mode driver, CUDA toolkit 13.2), TP8 (tensor-parallel) attention + EP8 (expert-parallel) MoE, vLLM 0.32.0's own release build with the FlashInfer release it pins (0.7.0.post1). The three source files of this PR (the kernel file, `DevKernel.h`, the fused MoE runner) were ported onto that release and copied into the patched arm's Python environment, which JIT-builds the module from them; the port differs from this PR only where the release lacks the feature (it has no 32-wide scale block, so the kernel's block-width check is dropped) and leaves out the new check in the batched GEMM runner (the release pins an older trtllm-gen export; the check does not affect timing). The baseline arm is the same environment with the released files. The activation the patched arm replaces, `activationDeepSeekKernel`, performs the same operations for the 128-wide scale block in the release and on `main` (`main`'s version adds the 32-wide branch of #8666, which this configuration never takes), so the gains below are gains against `main`'s kernel; the finalize kernels are the release's in both arms (the scalar `finalizeKernel` up to 32 requests, `finalizeKernelVecLoad` from 64). Both arms run with FlashInfer's autotuner off (`--kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=false`), so every GEMM uses the library's default tactic in both arms, each arm compiling FlashInfer into its own cache directory; the traces show identical kernel names in both arms apart from the activation (27 profiled windows per arm in each pair, none differing) and `activationDeepSeekKernelPersistent128` in every window of the patched arms. The cells, driven by `vllm bench serve` (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`): decode at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128 and 144 concurrent requests (8K-token random prompts decoded greedily to a fixed output length per cell; at TP8 + EP8 every rank's MoE call sees that many tokens per layer), 256 and 272 as context rows, beyond the headline range of 1 to 128 requests (288 would exceed our capture script's rule of 85 % of the KV cache at this prompt length), one 16K-token prefill chunk of a 32K prompt, and serving at 256 concurrent requests on ShareGPT with sampling (indicative). 72, 144 and 272 are the next measured points above 64, 128 and 256: they let the fixed-interactivity question, how many requests the patched build carries at the baseline's step, be read from measured steps. The step is the trace step period, the mean over the 8 ranks of the time between forward steps inside a profiled window (two windows per cell and arm, one for the prefill chunk); the unprofiled client step is the client's median time between output tokens in a second run of the same cell without the profiler. The GEMM column is the drift control: the two expert GEMMs run identical cubins in both arms, so their movement is the pair's noise. The two pairs' step changes agree within 1.1 points in the decode and context cells from 128 requests up (the indicative serving cell apart, see below) and within 2.4 points below, apart from the 64-request cell (4.1 points; see below). +    if controls:
+        # neighbouring experts far apart, so a lookup off by one GEMM tile would not match
+        alpha = 0.5 + 0.5 * (expert % 4)
+        beta = 0.25 * (expert % 3)
+        clamp = 1.0 + 1.0 * (expert % 5)
+    else:
+        alpha = beta = clamp = None
+
+    impl = FP8BlockScaleMoe(fp8_quantization_type=QuantMode.FP8_BLOCK_SCALE_DEEPSEEK)
+    weights = impl.quantize_weights(gemm1_weights, gemm2_weights, hidden_states)
+    inputs = impl.quantize_inputs(hidden_states, weights["hidden_states_scale_global"])
+
+    permute_info, scores = routing_reference_renormalize(
+        logits, TOP_K, NUM_EXPERTS, padding
+    )
+    top_k_indices = permute_info["topKIndices"]
+    is_local = (top_k_indices >= local_expert_offset) & (
+        top_k_indices < local_expert_offset + local_num_experts
+    )
+    permute_info["topKLogits"] = permute_info["topKLogits"] * is_local.to(
+        permute_info["topKLogits"].dtype
+    )
+    args = moe_args(
+        num_tokens,
+        NUM_EXPERTS,
+        HIDDEN_SIZE,
+        INTERMEDIATE_SIZE,
+        TOP_K,
+        padding,
+        inputs["hidden_states"],
+        inputs["hidden_states_scale"],
+        weights["hidden_states_scale_global"],
+        scores,
+        weights["gemm1_weights"],
+        weights["gemm1_scales"],
+        weights["gemm1_scales_global"],
+        weights["gemm2_weights"],
+        weights["gemm2_scales"],
+        weights["gemm2_scales_global"],
+        permute_info,
+        False,
+        ActivationType.Swiglu,
+        gemm1_alpha=alpha,
+        gemm1_beta=beta,
+        gemm1_clamp_limit=clamp,
+    )
+    reference, _ = run_moe_reference_dsfp8(args)
+
+    local = slice(local_expert_offset, local_expert_offset + local_num_experts)
+    kwargs = {}
+    if controls:
+        kwargs = dict(
+            gemm1_alpha=alpha[local].contiguous(),
+            gemm1_beta=beta[local].contiguous(),
+            gemm1_clamp_limit=clamp[local].contiguous(),
+        )
+    out = trtllm_fp8_block_scale_moe(
+        routing_logits=logits,
+        routing_bias=None,
+        hidden_states=inputs["hidden_states"],
+        hidden_states_scale=inputs["hidden_states_scale"],
+        gemm1_weights=weights["gemm1_weights"][local].contiguous(),
+        gemm1_weights_scale=weights["gemm1_scales"][local].contiguous(),
+        gemm2_weights=weights["gemm2_weights"][local].contiguous(),
+        gemm2_weights_scale=weights["gemm2_scales"][local].contiguous(),
+        num_experts=NUM_EXPERTS,
+        top_k=TOP_K,
+        n_group=None,
+        topk_group=None,
+        intermediate_size=INTERMEDIATE_SIZE,
+        local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+        local_num_experts=local_num_experts,
+        routed_scaling_factor=None,
+        routing_method_type=RoutingMethodType.Renormalize.value,
+        use_shuffled_weight=False,
+        weight_layout=WeightLayout.MajorK.value,
+        enable_pdl=True,
+        fp8_quantization_type=Fp8QuantizationType.DeepSeekFp8,
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert bool(is_local.any()), "some (token, slot) pair must land on this rank"
+    tolerances = impl.get_tolerances()
+    check_accuracy(
+        reference,
+        out.to(torch.float),
+        atol=tolerances["atol"],
+        rtol=tolerances["rtol"],
+        percent=tolerances["percent"],
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 8])
+def test_persistent_activation_empty_rank(num_tokens):
+    """No (token, slot) pair on this rank, the common decode case under expert parallelism.
+
+    The kernel is still launched (the grid comes from the host-side bound) and finds an empty
+    work list; it must write nothing and the call must give the same bytes with PDL on and off.
+    """
+    _skip_unless_sm100_class()
+    local_num_experts, local_expert_offset = EP_CASES[1]
+    inputs = _make_inputs(
+        num_tokens, local_num_experts, local_expert_offset, remote_only=True
+    )
+
+    def call():
+        return _run(inputs, local_num_experts, local_expert_offset, True)
+
+    out_pdl = call()
+    out_plain = _run(inputs, local_num_experts, local_expert_offset, False)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.isfinite(out_pdl.float()).all()
+    assert (out_pdl.float() == 0).all(), "no local expert contributes to any token"
+    assert torch.equal(out_pdl, out_plain)
+    names = cuda_kernel_names(call)
+    assert _launched(names, (PERSISTENT_KERNEL, OLD_KERNEL)) == [PERSISTENT_KERNEL], (
+        names
+    )
